current.text: Embiid is healthy entering the season. He had his first healthy offseason in years and reportedly added 15 pounds of muscle.
Yahoo lists him as questionable, with rest as the reason.
He has not looked great in the preseason.
The experts agree he should not go inside the top 50. Pick 43 is too early. The late 50s to about pick 60 is a fair spot to take a chance on him, especially if you have not taken risks earlier.
In an October 5 auction mock he went for 16 USD, and Josh would not pay that.
He is a high-risk, high-payoff pick. One expert gives him about a 10% chance of working out. Another says teams with Embiid will win their league if he stays healthy.
One expert expects him to finish around the 60s and expects more from him than last season. That expert calls his ESPN rank near 88 a steal.
He is expected to play about 40 to 50 games.
He is projected for about 33 minutes per game because he enters the season healthy.
He is the starting center next to Maxey, Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James.
Usage on the team is crowded. Maxey, Brown, LeBron and Embiid are expected to cut into each other's shots.

Mark projects about 20 to 25 points and about 10 rebounds per game, with some big scoring nights. He sees Embiid as a scorer who gets to the free throw line and rebounds while the others carry most of the scoring.
Mark projects about 51 to 52 wins for the Sixers and expects load management for the stars.
The Sixers have only 13 back-to-backs, but three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs. With a March 28 end, the team plays 3, 4 and 4 games in weeks 19 to 21.
Factor in the three playoff back-to-backs when you draft him, because he is not expected to play back-to-backs.

durable.text: He has had multiple meniscus surgeries on the same knee and has repeated knee problems. He is often listed as questionable and misses many games.
The experts do not trust him to get through a season. They expect the team to manage him, and Josh avoids him.
He has declined, but he still puts up great per-game numbers.
His blocks are well below his peak level.
Points and FT% on high volume are his big strengths. He gets to the free throw line often.
Turnovers are his weak category, even for a center.
As an often-injured player, he is worth a bit more in roto than in head-to-head.

note: Embiid is an elite per-game scorer and FT% anchor. He fits punt TO builds, but he only helps on the nights he plays, and he is projected for 49 to 54 games. The market cost is about 8 USD on both sites, far below the 24 USD he went for in our league last season. The experts' range (late 50s, never top 50, 16 USD was too much in a mock) suggests a price around 10 to 15 USD, with a top-end team behind him that can absorb missed games. Early in the season, check his rest pattern, his minutes (about 33 projected), and whether the weak preseason carries on. Keep in mind that the three playoff back-to-backs likely cut his weeks 19 to 21 to about 8 games.
